story.title: Trump Administration Appeals to Supreme Court Over California Ballots
story.summary: The Trump administration has filed an emergency application with the Supreme Court, seeking to block the counting of 20,000 mail-in ballots in California. The administration claims these ballots may belong to non-U.S. citizens, a claim that has been rejected by multiple courts and independent analyses. California officials warn that such a move could disenfranchise eligible voters.

explore_lenses.label: What is the administration asking the Court to do?
explore_lenses.title: A request to segregate, not cancel, ballots
explore_lenses.summary: The emergency request seeks to have California identify and hold aside mail ballots tied to the federal list until citizenship can be checked, rather than immediately invalidate those votes.

claims.text: The Justice Department's underlying complaint alleges that California and Los Angeles County sent mail ballots to people the federal government classified as likely noncitizens, and invokes 18 U.S.C. § 611, which bars noncitizens from voting in federal elections.

The federal government asked for ballots associated with people on its October list to be set aside and for citizenship to be verified before tabulation; it has characterized that as a preservation measure rather than a request to cancel ballots.
The Ninth Circuit denied the government's emergency request for an injunction pending appeal, finding that the government had not carried the required burden for that extraordinary relief.

explore_lenses.label: Why do officials dispute the 20,000-person list?
explore_lenses.title: The dispute centers on data reliability
explore_lenses.summary: California and Los Angeles County challenge both the federal list's accuracy and the feasibility of matching names on it to anonymous ballots already moving through the count. Federal officials maintain their immigration-record review supports the list.

claims.text: Los Angeles County told the court that, in a 200-record sample, more than half were canceled or inactive registrations and therefore had not been sent ballots; among records reporting a birthplace, just over 38% listed a U.S. birthplace.

A USCIS official disputed the county's birthplace inference, declaring that the agency's immigration-record review of those 200 people found none was born in the United States; the same official acknowledged approximately 189 records on the larger list had minor data discrepancies.

California election officials argue that eligibility changes must rest on verifiable information, not unconfirmed data matching; Los Angeles County also cited privacy and security concerns about the password-protected USB drive used to transmit the records.

The district court found the federal verification process insufficiently credible at the temporary-relief stage, describing substantial uncertainty about the methodology and warning that eligible voters could be disenfranchised.

explore_lenses.label: What happens if no emergency order issues?
explore_lenses.title: Ballot processing continues while the case proceeds
explore_lenses.summary: Without an emergency order, California's ordinary counting process continues; the underlying lawsuit is not thereby finally decided. Lower courts emphasized that the requested intervention would have to occur just before Election Day and amid ballots already being processed.

claims.text: The Ninth Circuit noted that the district court had appointed a special master to examine the voter-roll data and anticipated further proceedings after the November 3 election, meaning the factual dispute could continue even after the immediate election-period request becomes moot.

The Ninth Circuit majority said there was no feasible way shown to identify and segregate the specified ballots without risking major disruption to the tabulation system; Judge Patrick Bumatay dissented.
The government argues that once challenged ballots are commingled with other ballots, later relief becomes impracticable and alleged noncitizen votes could dilute citizens' votes.

Forecast: If the Supreme Court declines emergency relief, the state's count is expected to proceed under existing procedures while the lower-court litigation continues, because that is the practical consequence described by the Ninth Circuit's denial and the district court's post-election fact-finding plan.

story_report.summary: The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to intervene in a dispute over roughly 20,000 California mail ballots associated with people the federal government says may be noncitizens. It wants the ballots set aside while citizenship is verified before tabulation, describing the request as a preservation measure rather than an effort to cancel votes. The Ninth Circuit had already denied emergency relief, finding the government did not meet the required standard. Unless the Supreme Court changes that interim result, California’s count is expected to continue under existing procedures while the case proceeds.

sections.heading: Federal Challenge Targets Mail Ballots
sections.body: The Justice Department’s underlying complaint alleges that California and Los Angeles County mailed ballots to people the federal government classified as likely noncitizens. The government invokes a federal law barring noncitizens from voting in federal elections. It argues that allowing the challenged ballots to be commingled with other ballots would make later remedies impracticable and could dilute citizens’ votes. California officials, however, warn that the requested action could disenfranchise eligible voters.

sections.heading: Voter Data and Verification Disputed
sections.body: Los Angeles County told the court that, in a 200-record sample, more than half the registrations were canceled or inactive and had not received ballots. Of records reporting a birthplace, the county said just over 38% listed a U.S. birthplace. A USCIS official disputed that inference, saying an immigration-record review found none of the 200 people was U.S.-born, while acknowledging minor data discrepancies in about 189 records on the larger list. State and county officials have challenged the reliability and security of the federal data-sharing and verification process.

sections.heading: Lower Courts Leave Case Open
sections.body: The district court found substantial uncertainty in the federal verification methodology at the temporary-relief stage and warned that eligible voters could lose their votes. The Ninth Circuit majority also said the government had not shown a feasible way to identify and segregate the specified ballots without major disruption to tabulation; Judge Patrick Bumatay dissented. A special master has been appointed to examine the voter-roll data, and the Ninth Circuit anticipated further proceedings after the November 3 election.

unresolved.text: It remained unresolved whether the Supreme Court would alter the lower courts’ interim rulings before ballots were counted.
The merits record had not resolved whether any particular person on the federal list was ineligible or cast a ballot.

related_stories.title: Charges Dismissed Against Former FBI Officials in Hunter Biden Investigation
related_stories.summary: A federal judge has dismissed charges against two former FBI officials, Nicole Floris and Bradley Benavides, who were accused of lying to Congress regarding their knowledge of the Hunter Biden investigation. The judge expressed concerns about the handling of the case, citing issues of 'weaponization' within the Justice Department. Although the charges were dismissed, the Justice Department may still pursue a grand jury indictment against the officials.

related_stories.title: Democrat Haley Stevens Endorses Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan Senate Race
related_stories.summary: Democratic Congresswoman Haley Stevens has endorsed Republican Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate in Michigan, a move that has drawn criticism from her party. This endorsement comes just two days before the midterm elections and follows a public feud between Stevens and Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed over campaign ads. Stevens' decision is seen as a significant blow to El-Sayed's campaign.

related_stories.title: Trump Urges Republican Unity Ahead of Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: In a final campaign push at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, President Donald Trump emphasized the importance of the upcoming midterm elections, calling them 'the most important midterm I believe in our lifetime.' He acknowledged the historical challenges faced by the president's party in midterms but urged Republicans to unite and vote. Trump's remarks come as he campaigns alongside other candidates in a bid to bolster Republican turnout.
